ranked.headline: H&E histology and single-cell foundation models decode molecular tissue state
ranked.summary: Loki2, GenVinci and sc-HistoMorphomics treat routine H&E as a molecular readout, as Bloom, MCT and scUNVEIL scale cell representation learning.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is computational recovery of molecular state from tissue and cell data. Three preprints use H&E as a molecular readout. Loki2, trained on 15 million cells, tests how much molecular and cellular state histology encodes. GenVinci reconstructs 3D molecular tissue scenes and maps senescence across aging mouse organs and human skin. sc-HistoMorphomics links 194 nuclear morphometric features to spatial transcriptomics. In parallel, foundation models expand cell representation learning. Bloom unifies expression and chromatin accessibility across 300,000 mouse brain cells. MCT models cell sets to learn context-aware gene co-regulation. scUNVEIL pretrains on about 92 million human cells via next-UMI prediction. Spatial analysis tools include CIRCA, which uses causal representation learning to recover identifiable cell and niche programs, and spicyR v2, a permutation-free co-localisation test with sample-size estimation. Other work addresses dynamics and reliability: GFM for unseen perturbation responses, DRAFT for dynamic GRNs, GatorAnchor for neighborhood uncertainty, and SigMatch on tissue bias in disease-relationship predictions.

ranked.headline: Bioinformatics predictors face stricter benchmarks, calibrated uncertainty and general models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints expose benchmark leakage, embedding anisotropy and miscalibrated scores, while generic or consensus models match specialized tools.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluation discipline for sequence and structure predictors. Antimicrobial peptide classifiers lose their near-perfect scores once homology and length are controlled, and length alone separates benchmark classes. Protein language model embedding retrieval is benchmarked against MMseqs2 and Foldseek, with anisotropy degrading remote-homology search and ZCA whitening proposed as a remedy. ProtCOVER applies family-level conformal prediction to give valid coverage for missense variant effect predictors on unseen families. Infernal-GPU recalibrates Rfam E-values while recovering remote structured RNA homologs, and HyPhy 3's WALRUS jointly estimates alignment, phylogeny and selection to cut indel-driven false positives. A parallel theme favors generality over specialization: untuned TabPFN-3.5 matches or beats dedicated genomic prediction methods, and AbPoolRank's predictor-agnostic consensus over mixed structure pools reaches 58.0% Success@1 for antibody–antigen complexes. MicroDUET and FoldMapper extend foundation-model and homology-profile approaches to pathogen surveillance and inverse folding.

ranked.headline: DNA and RNA foundation models specialize inputs, probe variant effects, and drive design
ranked.summary: New preprints tailor pretraining to clades, methylation and ncRNA, test why personal-genome fine-tuning stalls, and design tissue-specific enhancers.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is DNA and RNA sequence foundation models moving from generic pretraining toward specialized inputs, diagnostic probing, and design. Several preprints narrow scope or enrich inputs. An apicomplexan model pretrained on 455 assemblies improves regulatory-signal prediction in data-sparse Plasmodium falciparum. ModBERT adds population variants and long-read CpG methylation. B-RANKO applies a 150M-parameter bidirectional decoder-only architecture to ncRNA. MARRI encodes opening penalties and hybridization gains for RNA-RNA interaction prediction. Other work examines what these models capture. Region-aware pooling over 5' UTR, CDS and 3' UTR outperforms global mean pooling in linear probes. LAMP attributes the failure of personal-genome fine-tuning to improve expression prediction to distal effects. Fine-tuned Borzoi and AlphaGenome perform comparably to, not better than, variant-based methods in admixed Latino whole blood. On design, GENECraft couples a genomic language model with a functional oracle without training. REGAL uses reinforcement learning over regulatory grammar to produce tissue-specific enhancers, validated across species.

ranked.headline: Transcriptional, epigenetic and post-translational modules tune ABA, JA and ROS in plants
ranked.summary: New Plant Physiology papers dissect specific regulators of ABA turnover, ROS signaling and JA-driven senescence across crops and Arabidopsis.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is mechanistic control of hormone metabolism and ROS signaling in stress and development. On the ABA axis, GhNAC029 represses GhNCED1 to lower ABA and drought tolerance in cotton. In Brassica, methylation of the BraCYP707A3.A02 promoter blocks BraBPC2.A08 binding, linking ABA catabolism to clubroot resistance. ANAC030 promotes Arabidopsis leaf senescence via JA biosynthesis, programmed cell death and chlorophyll metabolism. ROS-centred modules span contexts. In apple, MxMPK4-1 phosphorylates NADP-malic enzyme MxME3-7 at S201 to enhance ROS-mediated iron-deficiency responses. In pear, PUB8 degrades ZAT11/12, which activate LAC1 for ROS-linked lignification and stone cell formation. Post-translational and post-transcriptional layers recur: a preprint couples H2S persulfidation and PRMT5-dependent LSm4 methylation to alternative splicing in stomatal closure, and miR159a cleavage of BrMYB12 reduces myo-inositol/raffinose synthesis and thermotolerance. Ursolic acid limits fresh-cut apple browning through MdMYB70/MdbHLH62 control of ascorbate.

ranked.headline: Live-tissue spatial transcriptomics and multiomic profiling resolve stromal and tissue cell states
ranked.summary: New preprints add repeated sampling of living tissue, joint chromatin–isoform single-cell readouts and spatial causal models to cell-state mapping.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is methods for resolving cell states in tissue context, increasingly with temporal or regulatory depth. Two preprints introduce longitudinal spatial transcriptomics from living tissue: LIFE-seq samples repeatedly with nanoforest arrays to follow cortical injury in the same mouse, and LANCE-seq uses encoded microneedle arrays to profile mouse brain and track APAP-induced liver injury over time. Analytical layers extend spatial data. SpaceMACE refines tumour-cell calls using spatial proximity and expression similarity. Causal discovery on human liver Visium data models the causes and effects of senescence markers. FULL-seq jointly profiles chromatin accessibility and full-length transcripts per cell, linking promoter regulation to alternative first exon usage. A stromal strand runs alongside. Paired bulk, snRNA and chromatin profiling describes a continuous synovium–infrapatellar fat pad stromal continuum. Separately, HIPPO competency and oxidative metabolism mark human stromal clones with high bone-forming capacity. Modelling work identifies mixed feedback networks as the most robust topologies for restoring population heterogeneity.

ranked.headline: Cell-type and stage-resolved profiling maps early molecular lesions in neurodegeneration
ranked.summary: New preprints resolve neurodegeneration by cell type, age and stage, from synaptic proteomes to somatic mutation, interactomes and variant function.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is high-resolution molecular profiling of neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disease, with several items emphasizing age or stage. In R6/1 Huntington mice, cell-type proteomics shows excitatory synaptic protein loss and reduced glial neuronal support before motor onset, while aged TgHD minipig putamen shows age-dependent transcript and protein changes, including reduced D2 neuron markers. In ALS motor cortex, neuronal somatic mutation burden is higher in younger donors, with an SBS5 signature. A TDP-43 APEX2 atlas finds interactome remodelling persisting after stress granule clearance. A GBA1 assay maps glucocerebrosidase activity for over 10,400 variants. SETX loss in iPSC motor neurons shows stage-dependent effects, and 22q11.2 neurons show reversible mitophagy deficits. Fmr1-KO synapse profiling adds cell type-specific remodelling. Not all items concern aging.

ranked.headline: Stress triggers selective autophagy and condensate responses that remodel organelles
ranked.summary: New work links specific adaptors, lipid regulators and condensates to organelle turnover across ER, mitochondria, peroxisomes, lysosomes and endosomes.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is stress-responsive organelle remodeling, mostly via selective autophagy and its regulators, though the items span different compartments. Preprints describe Contact-phagy, in which SIGMAR1-CCPG1 turns over ER-mitochondria contact-site subdomains, and Mdm1, an ER-vacuole tether that balances phospholipid and neutral lipid metabolism to allow autophagosome completion in yeast. Another preprint ties NRF2 activation and autophagy to clearance of lipofuscin-like granules in RPE cells. Published work links iron deficiency to pexophagy through GABARAP-FLCN/FNIP1 activation of TFEB and TFE3, shows processing bodies collaborating with stress granules after lysosomal damage, and places RAB11-RAB30 on endosomes using a phosphoinositide switch. New here are the specific adaptors, tethers and condensates assigned to each stress context.

ranked.headline: Brain dynamics reorganize across states, expertise, and tasks along low-dimensional, flexible configurations
ranked.summary: Seven preprints show fMRI and EEG measures of dynamics, entropy, and coupling tracking altered states, expertise, and cognition in November 2026.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is that brain activity is characterized as state-dependent dynamics on a constrained structural or low-dimensional scaffold rather than as fixed regional function. Breathwork and jhana EEG studies report desynchronization, flattened hierarchy, and increased entropy complexity, with jhana complexity dissociated from experiential measures. Dance expertise is linked to higher local brain entropy and shared responses. Structure-function coupling varies with cognitive state, strongest during movie-watching and weakest under working memory load. Oddball detection follows shared low-dimensional brain-state dimensions with modality-dependent later trajectories. Meta-analytic work frames the self as shifting coalitions of distributed systems, and HCP resting-state data link spatial and temporal organization to trait-like dynamics. Evidence is preprint-only and spans heterogeneous methods and samples.

ranked.headline: Plant immune elicitors and receptors define systemic, cell-death and antiviral responses
ranked.summary: New work links peptide and pathogen elicitors to receptor sensitivity, NLR-dependent cell death, and SAR across crop and model plants.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how plants perceive diverse elicitors and convert them into immune outputs. A Nicotiana systemin study reports four new bioactive systemins detected by SlSYR1 and a premature stop codon in SYR1 orthologs of LAB N. benthamiana, explaining lineage-specific insensitivity. UvWSC1 from Ustilaginoidea virens triggers OsCPK13- and SOBIR1-dependent cell death, while SCMV HC-Pro triggers ADR1/NRG1-dependent hypersensitive death modulated by P3N-PIPO. N-hydroxypipecolic acid is reported to trigger SAR against wheat leaf rust. Arabidopsis UGT74F1 and UGT74F2 restrict turnip mosaic virus independently of salicylic acid, jasmonate and RNA silencing. A mild SCMV vector for maize is a methodological addition rather than part of this immunity thread.

ranked.headline: MRI structure and intrinsic signal dynamics track age, cognition and clinical status
ranked.summary: Seven preprints link MRI-derived structure and resting signal variability to development, aging, sensory and reading differences, and adversity-related psychosis risk.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is MRI phenotyping that relates individual differences in brain structure or intrinsic signal dynamics to age, cognition and clinical status. Several preprints examine moment-to-moment properties rather than mean activation: BOLD variability and altered brain-behavior covariance in adults with dyslexia, lower resting entropy in right superior temporal gyrus in hearing loss, and age-related changes in resting signal measures tied to inhibitory control, especially contextual control, in youths aged 8–18. Structural studies span the lifespan: nonlinear, region-specific cerebellar atrophy (strongest posteriorly, with midlife vulnerability) in 1,371 adults, and choroid plexus volume that rises with age and is larger in males across 700 manual segmentations. In adolescents, symmetric ACC sulcal patterns relate to lower proactive and greater reactive control. Bullying victimisation alters medial occipital white matter maturation and moderates FA–psychotic-like experience links. Samples outside the aging and choroid plexus datasets are modest (52–101 participants).

ranked.headline: Transcriptomic and proteomic readouts shift with cell compartment, scoring method and depth
ranked.summary: Seven preprints show that rankings and contrasts in omics readouts depend on evaluation depth, scoring, compartment and composition, not only on the underlying biology.
ranked.synthesis: Most of these preprints show that quantitative omics inferences are conditional on the context in which they are evaluated. Proteomic co-abundance method rankings change with evaluation depth, and colorectal fibroblast-epithelial stress granule contrasts depend on scoring method and depth. Post-stroke efferocytosis transcript signals are bounded by cell composition and time rather than flux. Cochlear ageing shows weak systemic concordance and a distinct macrophage programme. Cortical GABAergic channel expression aligns with dendritic conductance load in a reinforcing direction. A cell-state-conditioned sequence model predicts responses to an unseen stimulus but not stimulus-dependent genetic effects. The ImmunoTwin study reports a replicated coupling of T-cell exhaustion and macrophage M1 programs under checkpoint blockade. Together these point to explicit reporting of depth, scoring and compartment.

ranked.headline: Sequence models and QTL frameworks map noncoding variant effects across cell types and ancestries
ranked.summary: New preprints pair sequence-to-function predictors with eQTL and ancestry-aware analyses to resolve context-specific regulatory variant effects at disease loci.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is resolving how regulatory variants act in specific cellular and genetic contexts. AlphaGenome 2 predicts cell-type-specific regulatory activity and variant effects from 1-Mb sequence, while ChromBPNet models across 17 hematopoietic cell types score 302,830 variants and show lineage-structured accessibility effects. Empirical work shows ancestry shapes allele-specific expression in admixed whole blood, with 52 ancestry-associated loci replicating. Applications to disease include CAS-X, which integrates fine-mapped eQTLs across five metabolic tissues for type 2 diabetes effector genes, and PrediXSKAT, which weights rare coding variants by predicted cis-regulated expression. The endometriosis study shows cell-state prioritization depends on marker definition and donor structure. A Mendelian randomization study of midkine in pancreatic cancer is more loosely connected.

ranked.headline: CRISPRi knockdown responses prove context-dependent, limiting transfer across cohorts and cell lines
ranked.summary: New preprints quantify how poorly CRISPRi and drug-perturbation transcriptional responses generalize across cell lines, cohorts and datasets.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is quantifying how far perturbation responses generalize. CRISPRi Perturb-seq of essential genes in four human cell lines gives a median cross-line response correlation of 0.52, and transfer to a new line needs about 30% of it screened. Rejuvenation rankings from CRISPRi screens shift with the aging cohort and track cell growth programs, which suggests proliferation confounding. A comparison of six drug-perturbation resources finds high treated-expression agreement but limited concordance of drug-induced responses across sources. Related methods papers address technical confounding and prediction: cross-modal batch correction, DeepRNAi for siRNA on- and off-target activity, and ARC-Impute for spatial gene imputation. These are adjacent rather than CRISPRi-specific.

ranked.headline: Single-cell and long-read methods resolve somatic L1 insertions, structural variation and epigenetic heterogeneity
ranked.summary: New preprints pair single-cell and long-read assays to quantify somatic L1 retrotransposition in neurons alongside other genomic and epigenomic variability.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is measuring somatic and inter-individual genomic variation at single-cell or single-molecule resolution. LUSTRE maps L1 insertion sites in ~17,600 adult human neurons to estimate somatic retrotransposition rates. Related items extend this theme to other layers: assembly-independent k-mer estimation of Yq12 satellite size across 1,597 males, ChIMe-seq joint profiling of histone modifications, DNA methylation and nucleosome positioning, and COMET assignment of bulk long-read reads to cell types by methylation. Others characterize variability itself: genome folding differences between pluripotent and differentiated cells, and continuous karyotypic fluctuation in acral melanoma linked to MMBIR repair. These are heterogeneous in system, but share a move toward resolving variability that bulk or assembly-based approaches obscure.

ranked.headline: Transcriptional and cis-regulatory modules tune cell wall, organ form and stress tolerance in grasses
ranked.summary: New work links transcription factor modules and regulatory variants to xylem wall patterning, rice root and panicle architecture, and drought and salt tolerance.
ranked.synthesis: The items share a focus on discrete regulatory modules that set organ morphology and physiological performance, mostly in rice and other grasses. A single-cell xylem atlas identifies ZHD3 and ZHD4 as central regulators of protoxylem secondary cell wall morphology. In rice, OsWOX11 promotes thick AR2 adventitious roots, and a promoter variant (Hap3) shows higher activity. CArG-box deletions near APO1 quantitatively increase panicle secondary branching, pointing to recurrent cis-regulatory change. RLC3 pairs with KNOX proteins to activate lignin genes, controlling leaf rolling and drought tolerance. In creeping bentgrass, dosage-sensitive miR164-NAC tuning separates growth, drought and salt responses via AsNHX1. Together, these studies emphasize quantitative regulatory variation and secondary wall programs as levers on architecture and stress tolerance.

ranked.headline: Protein language models are adapted to narrow tasks with dynamics, structure and reaction context
ranked.summary: Six preprints adapt protein language models to variant effects, PTMs, kcat, methyltransferases, remote homology and nitrogenase activity using task-specific inputs.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is specializing protein sequence representations for defined prediction tasks by adding task-relevant information rather than relying on generic embeddings. DynamicsPLM augments a 35M-parameter model with molecular dynamics heads for zero-shot variant effects. HieraPTM combines sequence, language model and 3D structure features to move from PTM site recognition to functional phosphosite prediction. EnzRef treats reactants and products separately against a frozen model for kcat. S-PLM-TM uses a structure-aware model for sequence-only remote homology search. SMSTPred applies embeddings to methyltransferase substrate specificity, and CarmnaDD predicts nitrogenase activity from sequence with dual descriptors (R2 0.60, AUC 0.94). The items are heterogeneous in task, but converge on compact, targeted adaptation.

ranked.headline: Automation and computation link neuronal molecular identity to morphology and connectivity
ranked.summary: Five new reports scale Patch-seq, atlas-based identification, expansion microscopy and spatial transcriptomics, while a Drosophila study ties one isoform to identity.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is scaling quantitative neuronal characterization through automation and computation. Patch-seq work reports that detergent-cleaned reusable pipettes, robotic nucleus extraction and sonication preserve electrophysiology and transcriptomic yield. In C. elegans, probabilistic atlases built from near-wild-type strains raise variability-aware identification to 86.3% top-1. Whole-bulb light-sheet expansion microscopy with automated segmentation quantifies thousands of olfactory glomeruli in intact mouse bulbs, and SCOUBI maps axon-dendrite interfaces from extrasomatic transcripts in spatial transcriptomics. The Drosophila study is a mechanistic counterpoint rather than a throughput method: the broad-z4 isoform reprograms LPLC2 toward an LPLC1-like type, changing morphology, connectivity and transcriptome. The items differ in organism and approach but couple molecular identity to structure and connectivity.

ranked.headline: Notch, SOX9 and tissue architecture govern progenitor organization in the developing brain
ranked.summary: New preprints link Notch and SOX9 signaling and rosette morphogenesis to progenitor maintenance, while a 3D spheroid platform enables quantitative phenotyping.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how signaling and tissue architecture organize neural progenitors in early brain development. A SOX9-high radial glia program, regulated by Notch and SOX9, is reported to link progenitor maintenance to neuronal identity. Conditional loss of Rbpj in mice disrupts ventricular zone integrity and polarity, obstructing CSF flow and causing neonatal hydrocephalus. In human cortical organoids, neural rosettes are shown to arise from an interconnected tubular network formed by neuroepithelial folding and internalization. A whole-mount 3D imaging platform for dorsal forebrain spheroids detects altered growth and rosette phenotypes in an isogenic Down syndrome model. The zebrafish meninges work, implicating Foxc1 and Wnt, is adjacent rather than centered on progenitor organization.

ranked.headline: Trait evolution and diversification rates vary across lineages through lability, drift and gene flow
ranked.summary: New work links lineage diversification to labile traits and demography, from Mimosa niche shifts to drift in island kingfishers.
ranked.synthesis: The items address how selection, drift and ecological context structure phenotypic and lineage diversity, with no single mechanism dominating. Mimosa shows a continuum of diversification rates, with radiations accounting for most diversity and disparity and tied to abiotic niche lability. In island kingfishers, faster plumage color evolution tracks faster diversification and accelerates as genomic diversity declines, implicating drift. Bark anoles show convergent signaling traits decoupled from genomic species boundaries, with gene flow shaping speciation outcomes. Analysis of iridescent plumage across 3,151 bird species supports both Darwinian and Wallacean explanations for sexual dichromatism. In leaf-footed bugs, sexual dimorphism is labile and often arises already dimorphic in new traits. Together they emphasize lability and demographic context over uniform selective explanations.

ranked.headline: RNA splicing and mRNP maturation resolved by timing, modular assembly and chemical perturbation
ranked.summary: New preprints and a JCB paper resolve splicing timing, mRNP modules and spliceosome perturbation, extending RNA processing into cell-state and chemical contexts.
ranked.synthesis: The items treat RNA maturation as a process defined by timing and composition. In Drosophila spermatocytes, Y-loop A co-transcriptional splicing occurs in chromatin hubs, with delays varying by transcription cluster and increasing with maturation. In yeast, nuclear mRNPs share a minimal Yra1p/Pab1p core, while most factors bind transiently in stage-specific modules shaped by intron class and promoter. Splicing is also tied to cell-cycle control: SF3b1 and other factors relocalize to abscission checkpoint bodies, and timely abscission depends on splicing. The new element is direct perturbation and fractionation-based readouts: the covalent glue HL-1B stabilizes TOE1 on the spliceosome, altering snRNA 3'-processing and splicing, while zebrafish fractionation RNA-seq links RNA insolubility to ribosome, poly(A) tail and m6A features. The zebrafish study addresses RNA phase behavior more than splicing.

ranked.headline: Targeting lncRNAs and REV-ERB alters transcriptional programs in cancer cell models
ranked.summary: Preprints now link direct lncRNA targeting and REV-ERB agonism to altered transcriptional programs in cancer and drug-response models.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is perturbation of RNA-based and transcriptional regulation in cancer and disease models. Two items target long noncoding RNAs: depleting NRF2-induced NMRAL2P reduces non-small cell lung cancer proliferation and increases cisplatin sensitivity, while CD44-DT binds PCNA and AR to promote p21 degradation and suppress senescence in prostate cancer, where an RNA-PROTAC drives chimeric ncRNA-mediated AR degradation. STL1267, a REV-ERB agonist, alters HIF-1α and REV-ERBα localization and an ATF4-linked metabolic program in CoCl2-treated HeLa cells. A single-cell RNA-seq study of iPSC-derived cultures from 49 individuals maps eQTLs and drug-response eQTLs for ALK inhibitor effects. The cervical cancer item contributes a 12-gene neuroimmune signature. The advance lies in direct lncRNA targeting and genotype-dependent drug-response mapping at single-cell resolution.

ranked.headline: Disease-linked dysbiosis profiles across gut, oral, and body-wide microbial ecosystems
ranked.summary: Preprints now link microbial signatures in gut, oral, and body-wide sites to pediatric IBD and Parkinson disease, with spatial and proteomic methods.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of microbial community measurements, rather than host signals alone, to distinguish disease states. Metaproteomic microbial-protein panels from the ascending colon outperformed human-protein panels in machine-learning diagnosis of pediatric inflammatory bowel disease. In Parkinson disease, stool and plasma profiles from 211 patients and 204 controls showed dysbiosis-linked differences tied to diagnosis and severity, and a five-site study of 150 participants reported weakening cross-site microbial coordination and reduced core taxa alongside cognitive impairment. MiSA offers a spatial statistical route to detect disease-linked dysbiosis in image-based oral biofilm data from peri-implant mucositis. The NCF1 analysis addresses a host genetic question in chronic granulomatous disease and is separate from the microbial thread. Novelty lies in spatial and multisite resolution and in proteomic readouts for disease classification.

ranked.headline: AAV gene replacement and base editing rescue cardiac and mitochondrial disease models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend AAV-based gene replacement and editing to cardiac and mitochondrial disease models with functional readouts in vivo.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is in vivo genetic correction in mouse disease models using AAV-based or compact editing delivery. Two preprints apply AAV gene replacement to mitochondrial disease: LRPPRC replacement in heart and muscle knockout mice restored cardiac expression, preserved OXPHOS, prevented cardiomyopathy and extended survival, while neonatal Polg replacement preserved respiratory chain activity, delayed motor deficits and extended lifespan. A single-AAV adenine base editor with a compact cardiomyocyte-specific promoter corrects an MYBPC3 mutation and reverses hypercontractility and hypertrophy. An engineered compact PAMless ParTasR variant with TREX2 co-expression improves mammalian editing efficiency and corrects a tyrosinemia mouse model. The RepoV enhancer-reporter study is a distinct methodological contribution in human iPSC-derived neural organoids. What is new is the pairing of compact delivery architectures with functional rescue readouts across cardiac, muscle and metabolic disease models.

ranked.headline: Genotype and environment jointly shape regulatory variation and stress-linked traits in crops
ranked.summary: Field, long-read, ionomic, and genome datasets now resolve how genotype, environment, and haplotype structure shape gene regulation and stress traits in crops.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that measured plant phenotypes and transcripts depend on genetic background, environment, and the analytical frame used to interpret them. In switchgrass, field sampling across Michigan and Texas maps eQTL and GxE effects on gene regulation, selection, and leaf phosphorus traits. Pearl millet lines grown under drought in Senegal show that foliar ionomic stability is linked to flowering and biomass. Long-read transcriptomics of heat-stressed tetraploid potato resolves haplotype-specific expression, a heat-inducible allele, and a nucleus-targeted HSP40 isoform. Wheat nodal root anatomy differs by culm position beyond root area scaling, and allometric correction with GWAS reveals genetic associations distinct across root traits. A parent-of-origin-resolved Granny Smith genome shows that matched references expose sun-exposure and cold-storage responses that other references miss. Together, these studies point toward haplotype-aware, environment-explicit designs in crop genomics.

ranked.headline: Quiescent fibroblasts and preadipocytes show senescence-like secretory programs
ranked.summary: Recent preprints dissect how metaplasia, cAMP signaling and secretory programs govern tissue recovery and fibrosis resolution.
ranked.synthesis: These preprints share a focus on how tissue-resident cells govern recovery, remodeling and secretion rather than on one pathway. The clearest mechanistic thread concerns fibroblasts: endogenous Gs-dependent cAMP production is required for spontaneous resolution of bleomycin-induced lung and skin fibrosis. Quiescent human fibroblasts and preadipocytes display a secretory program (QASP) that overlaps the senescence SASP, varying with induction method and oxygen. In chronic pancreatitis, CD73 deletion in metaplastic epithelial cells worsened fibrosis and immune remodeling, implicating metaplasia in tissue recovery. Separately, MLL4 loss in palatal mesenchyme causes gland hypoplasia linked to reduced Fgf10, SOX9 and Edar, while CSP5, a truncated Cav1 scaffolding peptide, reduces lung injury and mucus expression in mouse models. What is new is that quiescent cells adopt a senescence-like secretory state and that endogenous cAMP and CD73 shape resolution.

ranked.headline: Risk-linked mutations disrupt striatal dopamine and cholinergic transmission
ranked.summary: Recent preprints link autism, schizophrenia, and Parkinsonian models to altered striatal dopamine and cholinergic circuit function.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is altered neuromodulatory control of striatal output by dopamine and acetylcholine. In a TSHZ3-linked autism model, cholinergic-neuron deletion of Tshz3 reduces M1 muscarinic transmission onto striatal projection neurons, abolishing D1 versus D2 excitability differences. A 3q29 deletion model of schizophrenia risk shows elevated evoked dorsal striatal dopamine release via a PKC-mediated mechanism. In a 6-OHDA Parkinson's model, prolonged D1 receptor signaling loss makes direct-pathway neurons hyperresponsive to dopamine. Analysis of 55 psychiatric-patient dopamine transporter variants resolves seven phenotypic classes of dysfunction. Neuron-specific Aralar/AGC1 knockout adds a metabolic dimension, with dopaminergic and redox deficits rescued by β-hydroxybutyrate. The items differ in disease context and mechanism; the shared element is perturbation of striatal dopamine and cholinergic control across genetic, pharmacological, and variant-level models.

ranked.headline: SLC25A35 controls mitochondrial import of branched-chain keto acids
ranked.summary: Recent preprints place mitochondrial carriers and dynamics regulators at the center of tissue-specific metabolic control in muscle, liver, adipose and macrophages.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that mitochondrial substrate entry and organelle remodeling set tissue metabolic output. Two items identify SLC25A35 as the mitochondrial carrier for branched-chain keto acids (BCKAs), with MCT1 and MCT2 mediating cellular entry; one reports that import constrains hepatic BCKA handling, and another links BCKA uptake to adipocyte lipogenesis. MTCH2 is reported to support metabolic remodeling in muscle satellite cells, including differentiation, respiration and fatty acid oxidation. In myeloid cells, mDIC deletion shifts adipose macrophages toward an efferocytosis-associated state while preserving mitochondrial respiration. In KPC cachexia mice, muscle OPA1 overexpression or BNIP3 knockdown partly preserved mass and function, sex-dependently. The newest element is the transporter-level account of BCKA import; the remaining items extend mitochondrial remodeling to other cell types and disease states.

ranked.headline: MS workflows resolve complex dissociation, glycoforms, and single-cell proteomes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend low-input LC-MS, single-cell, and native MS methods to protein complexes and viral glycoproteins.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the development and benchmarking of mass spectrometry and single-molecule workflows that improve sensitivity, analysis, and molecular resolution. Trap column benchmarking addresses low-input LC-MS proteomics, comparing a NanoShield trap column family against PepMap and direct injection across bed length, flush direction, and pore characteristics. Software contributions include OSMSS, a no-code R Shiny application for differential abundance, phosphosite, and enrichment analysis, and SCP-Viz, a visual toolkit tested on dried, room-temperature-stored single cancer cell digests. On the molecular side, super-resolved mass photometry links successive binding events to individual complexes to reveal dissociation pathways, while DIA-ECCR native mass spectrometry resolves intact SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoform distributions and heparan sulfate binding across variants. Across these items, the advance is pairing resolution at the level of single molecules and intact assemblies with analysis tools usable by non-specialists.

ranked.headline: DREAM complex represses central spindle genes and restricts blastomere plasticity
ranked.summary: Recent reports link DREAM-dependent repression and mechanical force to fate and cell-cycle decisions in C. elegans and Drosophila.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how developing cells restrict fate and cell-cycle programs. In C. elegans, a high-resolution fate assay shows blastomeres stay competent for muscle fate until late 16E, with LIN-54/DREAM and MET-2 restricting this plasticity. Another C. elegans study reports that DREAM-mediated repression of central spindle genes (zen-4, cyk-4, spd-1) marks the endomitotic transition in the intestine and blocks cytokinesis. In Drosophila, mesoderm invagination and embryo-wide force transmission are linked to mitotic entry timing during gastrulation. Planarian work shows canonical Wnt signaling controls early proliferation and differentiation of neural, muscle and parenchymal tissues. The new element is the DREAM complex acting on both commitment and cytokinetic gene programs, while the mechanical and Wnt studies extend context-dependent control to proliferation timing and tissue differentiation.

ranked.headline: Copy-number variation resolved by long-read and pangenome genome assemblies
ranked.summary: Long-read assemblies and a 140-strain C. elegans pangenome expose copy-number variation that count-based models can infer over evolutionary time.
ranked.synthesis: Copy-number variation is the dominant thread, approached through long-read assembly, pangenome analysis, and evolutionary inference. Near-complete de novo PacBio HiFi genomes of recently isolated Malian P. falciparum isolates reveal full genome architecture, with telomere-related variation among its features. A 140-strain C. elegans pangenome shows hyper-divergent regions enriched for copy-number variable environmental response genes and identifies a novel anthelmintic resistance locus. A coalescent duplication network model infers gene copy number evolution from copy counts alone, applied to NB-ARC domain counts of NLR genes. The machine learning study of partially sampled pathogen phylogenies is methodologically distinct and shares only the broader pathogen-genomics context. Collectively, the new elements are sequence-resolved variation maps and count-based models of duplication history.

ranked.headline: Redox enzymes and ROS control plant germination, photosynthesis and stress responses
ranked.summary: A review of plant superoxide dismutase history meets new work on peroxide control of germination and peroxiredoxin-driven PSII recovery.
ranked.synthesis: The items converge on reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis as a regulatory axis in plants. A review traces plant superoxide dismutase research from 1969, covering ROS detoxification, compartment evolution and stress markers. Preprints extend this framework to specific contexts. Peroxisomal H2O2 homeostasis during PEG-induced water stress rebalances ABA and GA metabolism to slow Arabidopsis seed germination. Separately, 2-Cys peroxiredoxins interact with chloroplast FAD7/FAD8 desaturases to increase phosphatidylglycerol trienoic fatty acids that aid PSII recovery from high light. A published study of melatonin and selenium nanoparticles in soybean addresses salt stress through MAPK signaling, hormone balance and membrane lipid remodeling, a related but distinct stress-response thread. The shared advance is the linkage of redox state to hormone and lipid metabolism.

ranked.headline: Epithelial cells execute death, clearance, and migration programs during tissue repair
ranked.summary: Recent work resolves epithelial death, debris clearance, matrix remodeling, and stromal guidance during regeneration and wound repair.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how epithelial cells coordinate death, clearance, and movement during tissue repair. In the adult Drosophila gut, hypoxia primes enterocytes for apoptosis via AMPK-p53 and activates Upd-JAK-STAT in stem cells, with regeneration proceeding in a reoxygenation-dependent manner. In wing discs, neighboring hinge epithelial cells clear apoptotic debris through Draper-dependent efferocytosis, and Draper loss delays clearance. Apical extracellular matrix in abdominal morphogenesis shifts from anchoring stationary larval epithelia to supporting directional migration. A bioengineered intestinal epithelial-fibroblast model shows fibroblast alignment and contact guiding organoid epithelial migration and gap closure during wound repair. What is new is the linkage of stress-induced death, debris clearance, and matrix or stromal guidance to repair, though none of these items test the interactions directly.

ranked.headline: Sex chromosomes shape sex-biased gene expression in embryos and male mice
ranked.summary: Cross-species atlases and sex-chromosome manipulations now resolve sex-biased expression and dosage compensation during prenatal development.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how sex chromosomes and sex-biased transcription shape gene expression in developing and adult tissues. In male mice, loss of the Xist locus, despite near-absent Xist expression, produces minor metabolic and memory effects, implicating a female-associated locus in male phenotypes. In embryonic chickens, comparison of sex chromosome and gonadal hormone manipulations indicates that chromosomal sex effects dominate hypothalamic gene expression. A cross-species single-cell atlas spanning mouse and human prenatal development maps sex-biased expression and X-to-autosome dosage compensation. A separate study traces sperm lipids to the morula stage, adding a distinct paternal contribution to early embryo metabolism.

ranked.headline: Mutation-selection models link fitness landscapes to genetic load and epistasis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a Genetics paper extend mutation-selection theory to epistasis across environments, mutation rate evolution, and sex allocation.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how mutation-selection balance shapes fitness and its distribution across genotypes, environments, and life-history traits. Spectral theory for genetic load shows that load depends on how fitnesses align with mutation-matrix eigenvectors, extending Haldane-Muller results. A global epistasis model fitted to yeast data predicts how non-home fitness changes during adaptation across backgrounds and environments. A multi-locus model shows mutation rates evolving through indirect selection out of equilibrium, and being selected against under homogenising selection. A separate sex allocation model reports continuous stationary distributions of sexual phenotypes under the same balance. Together these works move the focus from equilibrium fitness values toward the dynamics and stationary distributions that mutation and selection generate.

ranked.headline: COPS5 loss activates transposons and arrests mouse spermatogenesis
ranked.summary: Recent reports link piRNA, H3K9me3, H2A.Z and RNA-binding protein pathways to tissue-specific control of gene expression and transposon silencing.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how chromatin and RNA-based mechanisms establish tissue-specific gene expression programs in germline and somatic tissues. In mouse germ cells, COPS5 loss downregulates piRNA pathway genes, reduces pachytene piRNAs, activates LINE1 and IAP transposons, and arrests spermatogenesis. In Drosophila female germ cells, IDC, STWL and PZG recruit SETDB1 via WDE to deposit H3K9me3 silencing at phf7, a locus-specific domain controlling female identity. Maize H2A.Z mapping links the variant to tissue-specific expression, enhancers and photosynthesis genes in leaf and endosperm. The Drosophila Marf1 study addresses an RNA-binding protein newly expressed in the male accessory gland and its integration into regulatory networks. Together these reports show specific factors directly governing silencing outcomes in defined cellular contexts.

ranked.headline: Combined heat with drought or phosphate stress reshapes chromatin and hormone signaling
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a proteomics study examine plant stress memory, chromatin regulation, and hormone signaling under combined and osmotic stresses.
ranked.synthesis: Across these items, the dominant thread is how plants integrate multiple abiotic stresses at the level of chromatin and hormone signaling. In potato, combined heat and drought alter chromatin accessibility and prime ABA biosynthesis via StNCED3 on repeated exposure. In rice, thermopriming produces a restrained, lower-entropy heat transcriptional response with H3K27me3 retention and memory chaperone expression. In Arabidopsis, combined heat and phosphate starvation drives organ-specific jasmonate changes, with JA-Ile rising in roots and JA falling in shoots. A separate proteomics study links REVEILLE8-like clock genes to osmotic and salt stress responses, altering photosynthesis and phenylpropanoid pathways. What is new is the emphasis on priming and organ-level divergence under stress combinations.

ranked.headline: Phylogenomic datasets probe discordance and hybridization across four lineages
ranked.summary: Genome-scale and gene-dense datasets are now being used to test discordance, hybridization, and single-origin hypotheses in difficult phylogenies.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is genome-scale data used to resolve relationships where gene trees and organellar or nuclear signals disagree. In Australian Gossypium, whole-genome phylogenomics finds plastid-nuclear discordance but little nuclear evidence of introgression, revisiting homoploid hybrid speciation. In Dipsacales, resequencing of 88 species resolves Linnina backbone relationships, with ILS-driven discordance and possible ancient gene flow. In Aizoaceae, phylotranscriptomics shows gene-dense data resolve major relationships, while short internodes limit resolution within the radiation. In flatfishes, whole-genome phylogenomics and synteny from 17 species support a single origin of body-plan asymmetry. What is new is the emphasis on data density and genomic context, with the Ice Plant result marking limits on what gene-dense data can resolve.

ranked.headline: Senescent cells map to cell-type and tissue niches in aging human and mouse organs
ranked.summary: Spatial and single-cell multi-omics now resolve senescence to specific cell types and niches across human and mouse aging tissues.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the resolution of aging and senescence at cell-type and spatial scale. In human ovary, single-cell and spatial multi-omics across menopause identify granulosa-cell remodelling and implicate HEYL in ovarian aging and senescence. In human omental visceral adipose, older adults show more senescent cells than obesity alone explains, with senescent stem/progenitor and mesothelial cells participating in multicellular signaling that impairs organ function and drives inflammation. A multi-omic spinal cord atlas in mice and humans links age-related changes and senescence markers to specific cell types. In aged mouse liver, senescent cells localize to spatial inflammatory niches (SenSpots) with distinct epigenetic senotypes, while p53 loss increases inflammation and metabolic damage and p53 activation by an MDM2 inhibitor is reported to reverse age-linked changes. What is new is the combination of cell-type resolution with spatial context and perturbation-linked evidence, which frames senescence as tissue- and cell-type-specific.

ranked.headline: Context-dependent interventions reshape C. elegans lifespan and stress responses
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published study test how diet, temperature, drugs and neuropeptides change C. elegans lifespan and proteotoxicity.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is that lifespan and healthspan outcomes in C. elegans depend on context, including temperature, diet and the stress-pathway branch engaged. Dietary human HSP90 supplied via E. coli extends lifespan and healthspan through DAF-16, SKN-1 and HSF-1 stress signaling. Developmental daf-2 knockdown extends lifespan at 15°C but not 25°C, and the requirement for skn-1 is temperature-dependent. Methionine restriction extends lifespan through intestinal UPRmt activation that requires PKC-1 and the neuropeptides INS-27, INS-34 and INS-35. Rapamycin delays amyloid-β-induced paralysis and extends survival in C. elegans Alzheimer's models without reducing amyloid burden. The items test different interventions and do not describe a single mechanism.

ranked.headline: Climate and aridity gradients track body size, skull, and microbiome variation
ranked.summary: Four preprints tie climate, aridity, and seasonal gradients to morphological and microbial variation across birds, marsupials, lemurs, and seabirds.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the association between environmental gradients (thermal conditions, aridity, seasonal rainfall and temperature) and organismal variation across taxa. Across 5,715 bird species in 513 genera, thermal similarity among congeners best explains variation in the strength of Bergmann's rule. In 30 Sminthopsinae marsupial species, relative auditory bulla size rises about 20% along an aridity gradient, which the authors interpret as skull adaptation to arid environments. A 10-month study of red-fronted brown lemurs in Ranomafana links seasonal rainfall, temperature and diet to shifts in gut microbial communities. A seabird study reports that individual foraging-effort response diversity correlates positively with colony population stability in two North Atlantic species. What is new across these preprints is quantitative linkage of environmental variables to traits at the species, individual, or community level, not a shared mechanism. The items establish correlations, and they do not establish causation.
